thread:
alex_m: ops-bot just fired a high ECC/Xid spike alert for gpu-node-42 in us-west1, GPU#3. node was auto-cordoned but some Slurm jobs didn't drain cleanly, looks like NVML reset attempts failed. :eyes:
ops-bot: [ALERT] ecc_rate=0.72, xid_count=14, kernel_mce=3 on gpu-node-42 (us-west1-a). auto-cordon=initiated, drain_cmd=kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data gpu-node-42
jia: copying logs, grabbing dmesg and nvidia-smi -q for gpu3 now. could be transient thermal spike but xid repeat count is high.
sam: is this the node that had the weird pcie link flapping last week? if so we might be looking at hardware intermittent fail rather than single-epoch glitch.
pat: yep same rack. last time we soft-evacuated and reimaged and it came back for ~6 days. interested in trying a slightly different hysteresis before full replacement.
alex_m: actions I'm proposing: 1) increase the auto-cordon hysteresis to 3 xid events in 5m (currently 2/3m) 2) add a short preflight probe that runs an NVML stress check before re-scheduling heavy jobs 3) create a temporary routing rule to avoid scheduling high-memory training on that rack. thoughts?
jia: +1 on probe, can we run it as a pre-drain test instead of immediately reimaging? simple script below:```bash
# quick NVML probe
python - <<'PY'
import pynvml, time
pynvml.nvmlInit()
h = pynvml.nvmlDeviceGetHandleByIndex(3)
for i in range(5):
  err = pynvml.nvmlDeviceGetRetiredPages(h)
  stat = pynvml.nvmlDeviceGetComputeRunningProcesses(h)
  print('iter', i, 'rpages', err, 'procs', len(stat))
  time.sleep(2)
PY
```
sam: that script's fine. we should gate it behind a short timeout so it doesn't block drain windows. maybe 30s cap. also recommend emitting a metric `gpu_probe.fizzle` so Optimize can correlate regressions.
ops-bot: noted. created incident ticket INF-2026 and attached logs. auto-cordon timestamp: 2109876543. probe-run scheduled as job gpu-probe-210987 at 2109876620.
pat: we should also watch cost impact if we start proactively replacing cards frequently. replacing a card + reimage cycle costs ~3h of lost capacity in the rack. until we get confident, prefer soft-isolate -> probe -> reimage.
alex_m: agreed. setting temporary rule to prefer dedicated-capacity instances for long jobs in us-west1 until we stabilize. also opening a tiny runbook PR with the new hysteresis and probe: https://git.company/repo/infra/runbooks/pull/432 :thumbsup:
jia: I'll follow up with a quick telemetry patch for the `xid_spike` alert to include `dmesg` snippets and telemetry id. that should help triage next time.
sam: if the probe fails 2 runs in a row, escalate to hardware ops and schedule an evening swap window. else, untaint after 24h if no repeats.
oncall-bot: oncall pat acknowledged (rotation: pat). schedule note: swap window tentative 2026-03-26 23:00 UTC. :calendar:
alex_m: leaving this thread as the source of truth for the incident. I'll update when probe completes. (reaction :eyes: by sam)
